who gets burned

Sound familiar?

The solo founder

  • "I'm doing everything myself."
  • "Nobody else knows how this works."
  • "I can't step away for a day."
  • "I do not know where to start with delegating."

The business cannot grow past one person, so growth, a team, and personal goals all wait.

The person wearing every hat

  • "I'm the admin, the sponsorship lead, and the volunteer coordinator."
  • "Everything lands on me."

Nobody has defined which hat is whose, so there is no time left for family, goals, or thinking.

The small team with scattered tools

  • "Our contacts are in five places."
  • "Every event starts from scratch."
  • "Departments do not talk."

People re-enter the same information, and details slip between tools.

how I help put it out

Three moves, in this order.

1

Map how work really flows

Where it starts, who touches it, and where it gets stuck.

2

Define workflows and owners

Workflows, role outlines, and playbooks, gathered into one operations manual.

3

Build the tools around it

CRM, project space, and automations, set up to fit the process and handed off.

Tools come last. I pick software to fit your people and your process, and I only automate what already works by hand.

hi again!
the person behind the systems

I learned operations by organizing people first.

It all began in Wisconsin. In high school I was a Next Actor in the student camp at Next Act Theater, and I have been absorbed in nonprofit work ever since. After college I came back to that camp as the assistant teacher and helped oversee it.

In college I leaned into organizational leadership. I served on the Black Student Union Executive Board, started my own a cappella group and a women of color initiative on campus, and worked in the Department of Diversity and College Access, where I was the student manager overseeing student employees and worked the front desk and event support at the Multicultural Resource Center.

I moved to Austin in 2023 and started Right Hand Support Services. That path is how I grew into operations: I am the connective tissue between the people, the tools, and the plan, across every department I touch.

  • High schoolNext Act Theater student camp, then assistant teacher after college
  • CollegeBlack Student Union Executive Board, a cappella group, women of color initiative, Department of Diversity and College Access
  • 2023Moved to Austin and started Right Hand Support Services
  • NowFractional operations management, consulting, and project management

On stage and on mic

I have spoken on podcasts and panels, performed live music, and acted on stage. Comfortable in a room, comfortable with a microphone.

Giving back

I like to volunteer and spend my time with aligned organizations, giving back what I can. I often volunteer at conferences and start initiatives like Women in Cups.

Get to know me off the clock

I am an old school jammer. Give me music from the 60s, 70s, 80s, and 90s and I am happy, especially at karaoke. Add a good plate of Ethiopian or Mexican food and I am set. I paint, I do makeup looks (special effects included), and I stay grounded through my spirituality. At home it is two cats, and a baby on the way.
